summary: The fleet orchestrators, snapshot provider, audit, fleet report and alerts existed only as library code. Operators had no way to dry-run a registry of accounts. This adds `run.py --fleet-dry-run --registry PATH` with optional `--concurrent N`, `--fleet-journal-dir DIR` and `--identity-salt-env NAME`.  sdk/fleet/factory.py builds each account's context from the environment. A profile's credentials_secret names either <NAME> (an auth string, the --auth-file format) or <NAME>_EMAIL/<NAME>_PASSWORD (the --login-email flow and the daily workflow's PSS_ACCOUNT_<n>_* secrets). Login reuses Client.login. Credential values never reach output, journals or error text: exceptions are re-raised with the account's values replaced and secret-shaped text redacted. Each account gets a device that never touches the shared ./.device file, and its own HTTP session instead of the class-level one. Room, research and hull designs come from read-only calls (listAllDesigns4 for ShipDesign; hulls stay empty and are noted when it fails).  The command only ever calls run(execute=False). It writes one <alias>.log journal per account, then prints an accounts table, the fleet report and the alerts with the isolation audit. It exits 2 on registry, salt or journal-dir errors, otherwise 0. Tests use fake clients with sockets patched to raise. Implemented by the integration specialist subagent in an isolated worktree, independently reviewed by the verifier subagent (CHANGES-REQUIRED, then APPROVE-WITH-NITS; credential/id leaks and nits fixed in 328bcc5 and 1e8481d), and re-validated by the parent.
